entities.summary:
Messenger, launched by Meta Platforms (formerly Facebook, Inc.) in August 2011 as a standalone instant messaging application, fundamentally reshaped global digital communication by detaching the messaging function from the primary Facebook social network. Originating as Facebook Chat in 2008, its evolution into a dedicated service under the leadership of Mark Zuckerberg responded to the burgeoning smartphone market and the user demand for immediate, pervasive connectivity. This strategic unbundling allowed Messenger to compete directly with emerging messaging platforms, cementing its role as a ubiquitous tool for interpersonal and increasingly, commercial interaction across continents.

Initially offering basic text messaging, Messenger rapidly expanded its feature set to include voice and video calls, group chats, file sharing, and integrated payment functionalities. By 2017, the platform boasted over 1.2 billion monthly active users, a testament to its aggressive integration with the Facebook ecosystem and its continuous innovation in user experience. Key developments included the introduction of 'Messenger Day' (stories), chatbots for automated customer service, and end-to-end encryption options, though the latter's rollout has been gradual and incomplete across all functionalities, sparking ongoing debates about user privacy and data security.
